title: Fix wall-clock budget overshoot in claude-launcher.windows.test.ts control-poll-slice assertion
description:
Filed by governor-e01ddc57 on 2026-08-19 with the human's explicit approval (v0.2-freeze scope action).

DEFECT: packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-launcher.windows.test.ts:237 ("stays alive beyond the control poll slice") asserts a wall-clock bound of 3000ms that overshoots under full-suite load: measured red ~2/8 runs inside the full suite (AssertionError: expected 3637.63... to be less than 3000), 0/6 red in isolation (worker-21246c33, 2026-08-19, healthy host — spawn probe ~20-25ms, so NOT the spawn-cliff class). QA re-run at 21:19Z did not reproduce it, consistent with the ~2/8 rate. Same defect family as the release-archive-cleanup 5000ms finding (sibling task): a timing-sensitive assertion budgeted for an idle host, red only under suite parallelism, so it goes quiet whenever the host is fast and resurfaces as a phantom red attributed to whoever runs the suite next.

Fix shape is the owner's call: poll-count/event-based bound instead of wall-clock (see tests/e2e/foundation/orphan-reap.ts pidReaped pattern and the e2e-harness no-wall-clock guard for prior art), or an honest budget derived from measured suite-load latency — NOT a bare constant bump chosen to make the red go away.
definitionOfDone: The line-237 assertion no longer fails under full-suite parallelism: 8/8 green in full-suite runs on a healthy host (spawn probe cited, tens of ms)
The bound is either event/poll-based or a documented budget with its derivation in a comment; no bare magic-number bump
Test still fails (drill) when the launcher genuinely outlives the control poll slice - kill the mechanism once and restore byte-exact to prove the assertion is live

Verified coordinates: PROVIDER_DELAY_MS=150 (:32), LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS=6_000 (:38), CHILD_DRIVEN_BOUND_MS=3_000 (:51, exactly timeout/2, derivation comment :40-50), WATCHDOG_MS=10_000 (:55), the bound assertions at :237-238, the child-outlived-the-slice guard at :233-234 (elapsedReport, child-written elapsed >=100ms), it() timeout 25_000 (:243). THE INVARIANT the fix must preserve (comment :47-50): the truthClass/observation assertions CANNOT catch the regression — a broker that returns PROVEN only after the parent tears its endpoint down satisfies all of them; only latency distinguishes "the child was observed" (~960-990ms idle, 3637ms measured under full-suite load) from "the timeout was waited out" (>= LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS, ~6490ms measured). KEY STRUCTURAL FACT for the fix: the defect path takes >= the CONFIGURED timeoutMs BY CONSTRUCTION — the broker cannot return early in the defect scenario — so a bound tied to LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS discriminates mechanically, independent of host speed. Confirm the file is untouched since the filing (git log -1 -- <file> → abc3dcf era) and record a healthy-host spawn probe (git --version x5, tens of ms — admissibility precondition for every timing number in this task).

This is what makes a timeout-derived bound host-speed-independent: correct path ~1s (idle) / 3.64s (measured under suite load) vs a defect floor pinned to the SET constant.

INVARIANT THE FIX MUST PRESERVE: latency is the ONLY discriminator. truthClass/observation assertions are satisfied by a broker that returns PROVEN late (:47-50), so the fix keeps a latency bound and only re-derives it. Corollary confirmed against lifecycle.ts: a TIMEOUT terminal maps to reason ["CLAUDE_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT","LAUNCHER"] (:65), but the guarded regression is the PROVEN-but-late shape that never reaches that mapping.

implementationPlan.description: IMPLEMENT THE LOAD-IMMUNE BOUND (no bare magic-number bump — reopenReason binding). GOVERNOR AMENDMENT to this task's fix-shape guidance (supersedes the description's "event/poll-based bound preferred" line; ruling msg-43a4f6f5 → this comment, 2026-08-19 21:45Z).

worker-21246c33 read the file before planning and the description's preferred shape is WRONG for this test:

1. LATENCY IS THE DISCRIMINATOR, not an incidental ceiling. The file's own header (claude-launcher.windows.test.ts:39-51) documents it: correct behaviour ~959-993ms, defect signature ~6,490ms, and "LATENCY IS THE ONLY ASSERTION that can tell 'the child was observed' from 'the timeout was waited out'". A broker that eventually returns PROVEN after parent teardown satisfies every truthClass assertion — only the clock catches it.
2. POLL-CONVERSION IS DISALLOWED: production exposes no watchdog/completion-cause signal (WATCHDOG_MS lives only in the test-side Promise.race helper, :70-82); converting to polls would require adding a production poll counter — a production change on a test-hardening task.
3. ADMISSIBLE BOUND RANGE IS EXACT, not taste: any bound >= 6,490ms is blind to the defect — reject on sight. A flat raise into 4,500-5,000 is evidence-admissible (still ~1.5-2.0s clear of the defect, survives the measured 3,637ms overshoot) but weak.
4. PREFERRED SHAPE: bound relative to a same-run calibration baseline (k x measured launcher pin cost) — moves with the host while keeping child-driven-vs-timeout-driven discrimination. Whatever ships, KEEP the positive control at :233-234 (elapsedReport >= 100); without it the test degrades into the vacuous child-exited-early version.
5. This file carries its OWN 25,000ms test-level timeout — vitest's inherited default is NOT the mechanism here, unlike sibling task-59c16705 where it is. Same symptom family, different root causes: do NOT share one plan template across the two rows.

DoD reading under this amendment: DoD item 2's "event/poll-based" arm is void; its "documented budget with derivation" arm is the live one, with the derivation bounded by items 1-4 above. DoD items 1 and 3 unchanged.
